transcript.text: Good morning everyone. Before we get into the details of the "Tidal Memory" installation plan for Gallery 4, I want to make sure we go through our standard final check. I need to hear from each of you — rights, technical, accessibility, and artist representatives — on whether there are any conditions that need to be added to this draft plan before I can approve it. The current proposal has online-connected playback, eight visitor stations, 15-minute sessions, and a 5:00 PM public opening on October 12. Please let me know where everyone stands.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical rights condition. I reviewed the countersigned music license this morning, and it imposes three conditions that are not yet reflected in the draft plan: First, Tidal Memory may be exhibited only through offline local playback — not online-connected playback as currently proposed. Second, visitors may not photograph or record the installation. Third, the exact credit line 'Music licensed from Harborlight Editions' must be used. These conditions need to be added to the plan before I can sign off on rights clearance.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical technical condition. I completed the headset and network test after yesterday's installation rehearsal, and the results show that the approved headset model supports only six simultaneous stations — not the eight currently proposed. Additionally, each session must be limited to exactly 12 minutes rather than 15 minutes to prevent thermal shutdown. The test report is still processing in the equipment vendor's queue, but these are hard technical constraints that must be reflected in the plan before I can sign off on technical clearance.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical accessibility condition. I confirmed with the festival's access consultant today that one of the six visitor stations must be a seated, step-free station. Additionally, every visitor notice must display the exact warning 'Flashing light and sudden sound.' I should note that the consultant's written confirmation was received after the draft visitor signage was already sent to print, so the signage will need to be reprinted with this corrected warning. These conditions must be added to the plan before I can sign off on accessibility clearance.
